overview.title: Morocco’s Mediterranean national park
overview.p1: Al Hoceima National Park protects a rare stretch of Moroccan Mediterranean coastline: high limestone cliffs, scrub-covered hills and a marine zone important for birds and sea life.
overview.p2: Many of the best coves are reached by boat or longer walks. Cala Iris and Torres de Alcalá sit on the park’s accessible edge and make practical gateways.
overview.p3: Go with water, sun protection and a local skipper or guide if you want hidden beaches rather than roadside viewpoints alone.

q1.question: Do I need a guide?
q1.answer: Not for every viewpoint, but boat trips and remote coves are easier and safer with local operators.

q2.question: Can I swim in the park?
q2.answer: Yes in suitable coves when sea conditions allow — never assume open-water safety.

q3.question: Best season?
q3.answer: Spring and autumn for hiking; summer for swimming if you accept heat and boat demand.

q4.question: How far from town?
q4.answer: The park shoreline starts west of Al Hoceima; plan transfer time into your day.

q5.question: Wildlife?
q5.answer: Birdlife is a highlight; marine sightings are possible but never guaranteed.
